rot.distant.ideia.ex1.e1: You already know key squares and direct opposition. Now the kings start further apart.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.e5: For this pawn, the key squares are f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.e6: Your king wants one of them; the black king wants g6, in front of the pawn, from where it watches all three.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! Your king goes to the black king's file and advances toward the key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to e4, on the black king's file, toward the key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c2.1: With this move your king retreats, and Black finds a defence that holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c2.2: The black king goes to f7, heading for g6, in front of the pawn, from where it watches f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d2.1: With this move your king retreats, and Black finds a defence that holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d2.2: The black king goes to f7, heading for g6, in front of the pawn, from where it watches f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e2.1: Five squares, an odd number, but your king retreats, and Black gets in front of the pawn first.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e2.2: The black king goes to f7, heading for g6, in front of the pawn, from where it watches f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c3.1: With this move your king heads away from the pawn and the key squares, and Black holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c3.2: The black king goes to f7, heading for g6, in front of the pawn, from where it watches f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c4.1: With this move your king heads away from the pawn and the key squares, and Black holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c4.2: The black king goes to f7, heading for g6, in front of the pawn, from where it watches f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e3.1: Your king goes to the black king's file, but without advancing, and Black holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e3.2: The black king goes to e7 and faces yours, three squares apart with White to move: the opposition is Black's.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d4.1: Your king advances but leaves the black king's file, and Black holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to f7 and reaches f6 or g6 before your king; from there, it shuts the key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.g3g4.1: Pushing the pawn before the king does not work: Black holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.g3g4.2: With the pawn on g4, the key squares move up to f6, g6 and h6, and the black king, on f7, is already next to them.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn, and it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.fins.afogado: The black king has no move and is not attacked: it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always closes the way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: The black king always closes the way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l1: Notice: your king is on e4, on the black king's file, with three empty squares between them: e5, e6 and e7.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l2: Kings on the same file, with three or more squares between them: if the number is odd, it is distant opposition. With only one square, it is direct.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l3: To know who has it, count the squares between the kings. An odd number after your move: the opposition is yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l4: Why? If the black king advances, two squares remain; yours advances too, and one remains: the black king must give way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l5: Black has several defences. Let's start with the most common one.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king goes to f7, heading for g6, in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l7: Your king gets there first, to f5: a key square, facing the black king. It is direct opposition, and it is yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l8: Go back one move. What if your king went to f4, also toward the pawn?
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l9: The black king faces yours from f6, and the opposition passes to Black: it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l10: Let's go back to the main line, with your king on f5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l11: The black king goes to g7 and tries again to get in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l12: Now the pawn looks ready to advance. See what happens.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l13: With the pawn on g4, the black king faces yours from f7, and the opposition is Black's: it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l14: Go back one move. King first: it goes to g5 and faces the black king again.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l15: Your king goes to g5, another key square, facing the black king.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l16: The black king goes to f7, near the pawn's path, waiting for it to advance too early.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l17: The pawn still waits: if it advances now, the black king returns to g7, facing yours, and it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l18: Your king goes to h6, on the file next to the pawn's; going to f5 also wins. Now the pawn advances, protected by the king, and promotes.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l19: Let's go back to the position after the first move. What if Black goes to f8?
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l20: The black king goes to f8, and yours goes to f5, a key square: White wins the same way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l21: What if the black king goes to e7, on the same file as yours?
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l22: Your king goes to e5, facing it: direct opposition, and it is yours. Going to f5 also wins.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l23: But f4 does not work: the black king would go to f6, facing yours, and the opposition would pass to Black.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l24: Then follow the black king, always facing it, as far as g5, a key square. You already know the rest.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l24a: What if your king went to e2, also on the black king's file? It would leave five squares, an odd number.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l24b: But it retreats: the black king goes to f7 and reaches g6 first. The count only works with the king going forward, heading for the key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l25: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l26: Take your king to the other king's file, heading for the key squares, and leave an odd number of squares between them: the distant opposition is yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l27: The pawn only advances afterwards. Now let's see the defence: Black uses distant opposition too.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.e1: Now you play Black, and the board turns around. White has just taken the king to e3.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.e2: The white king wants f5, g5 or h5, the pawn's key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.e3: Your king must close that path, with the same weapon as in the attack: distant opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! Three squares between the kings, and you have just moved: the distant opposition is yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to e7, on the white king's file: three squares, and Black has the distant opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.alt.e8f7.1: That holds too: from f7, your king reaches f6 or g6, beyond the key squares, before the white king.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.alt.e8f7.2: Now let's go to the main line, with the king on e7.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8f8.1: With that move your king stays off the white king's file, and White can win.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8f8.2: The white king goes to f4: on your king's file, three squares apart with Black to move. The distant opposition is White's.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d8.1: With that move your king moves away from the pawn, and White can win.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d8.2: The white king goes to f4, next to f5 and g5; from d8, your king cannot reach those squares before it.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d7.1: With that move your king heads away from the pawn, and White can win.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d7.2: The white king goes to f4, next to f5 and g5; from d7, your king cannot reach those squares before it.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.coroa: The pawn promoted. Without the opposition, Black cannot hold.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.repeticao: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.capturado: The pawn fell: your king won the fight for the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: The black king has no move and is not attacked: it is a draw, and the defence held.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l1: White must give way. The most common try is to take the king to f4, next to the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l2: The white king goes to f4.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l3: You face it from f6: direct opposition, and it is still yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l4: Go back one move. What if your king went to f7, near the promotion square?
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l5: Between f4 and f7 there are two squares, an even number: the opposition passes to White.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l6: The white king goes to f5, a key square, and faces yours. The pawn will promote.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l7: That is why, against the king on f4, the answer is f6, facing it.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l8: With no way through for the king, White pushes the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l9: Your king steps to g6, in front of the pawn: the ideal spot for the defence. It is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l10: Let's go back to the position with your king on e7. What if the white king goes to e4, on your file?
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l11: You face it from e6: one square between the kings, and the opposition is still yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l12: Wherever the white king goes, your king faces it, and the key squares stay closed: it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l13: Let's go back to the position with your king on e7.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l14: Take your king to the other king's file, heading for the key squares, and leave an odd number of squares between them: the distant opposition is yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.ponte: Now I play both sides in three positions. Count the squares between the kings before each move.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.1: First position: the pawn is on g2, and the key squares are f4, g4 and h4.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.2: The kings are on the same file, with six squares between them, and White is to move.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.3: The white king goes to e2 and leaves five squares: an odd number, and White has the distant opposition.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.4: The black king advances, and four remain.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.5: The white king advances too and leaves three: odd again.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.6: The black king advances once more, and two remain.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.7: The white king leaves just one: it is direct opposition, and the black king must give way.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.8: Five, three, one: with every move, the odd number stays with White.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.9: The black king goes to f6, near the pawn.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.10: The white king gets into f4, a key square, facing the black king. The pawn will promote.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.11: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.distant.demos.cincoCasas.12: With more squares, the count is the same. We chose e2 because there your king stands on the black king's file and leaves five squares.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.1: Second position, now from Black's side, and the board has turned around. The pawn is on f2.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.2: The key squares are e4, f4 and g4, and the kings are on different files.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.3: The black king goes to c6, on the white king's file: three squares, and Black has the distant opposition.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.4: Going to d6 or e6 also holds: the black king stays close to the key squares.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.5: The white king goes to d3, toward the key squares.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.6: The black king faces it from d5: direct opposition, and it is still Black's.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.7: Wherever the white king goes, the black king faces it, as in the second example: it is a draw.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.8: Let's go back to the starting position. What if the black king went to e7, near the pawn?
rot.distant.demos.tempo.9: Now it loses: the white king goes to d3 and then to e4, a key square, before the black king can close the way.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.10: On e7, the black king does not take the distant opposition, and the white king reaches the key squares first.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.11: Now the same starting position, but with White to move.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.12: The white king goes to d3, on the black king's file: three squares, and White has the distant opposition.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.13: Same position, opposite results: whoever is to move takes the opposition. We say that side has the tempo.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.14: Let's go back to the defence, where Black was to move and the black king ended up facing White's, on d5.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.15: Take your king to the other king's file, heading for the key squares, and leave an odd number of squares between them: the distant opposition is yours.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.1: Third position: the same one, with White to move, but the white king goes to d2, not d3.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.2: Count the squares between the kings: now there are four, an even number.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.3: In the first position, the white king on the second rank worked: the black king was on the eighth, leaving five.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.4: Here the black king is on the seventh, and four remain. It advances to d6 and leaves three: the opposition passes to Black.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.5: Going to e6 also holds. Each time the white king advances, the black king faces it and shuts the key squares.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.6: The white king advances to d3 and leaves two squares, an even number.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.7: The black king faces it from d5. It is the same position we saw a moment ago, and it is a draw.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.8: Before every move, count the squares. If the other side left an even number, advance and leave an odd one.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.ponte: Your turn: one attack and one defence against the machine. Before every move, count the squares between the kings.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e3.1: Going to e3, your king goes to the black king's file, but leaves four squares between them: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e3.2: An even number: the opposition is Black's. The black king goes to d7, heading for c7, and nears the key squares first.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e2.1: Going to e2, your king leaves five squares, an odd number, but retreats and stays far from the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e2.2: Here the count is not enough: the black king leaves the file, goes to d7 and then c7, near the pawn, before your king.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.1: Going to f4, your king advances off the black king's file and does not take the distant opposition: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.2: The black king goes to d7 and then to c6, in front of the pawn: your king can no longer reach the key squares.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g4.1: Going to g4, your king moves away from the pawn and the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g4.2: The black king goes to d7 and then to c6, in front of the pawn: your king can no longer reach the key squares.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g3.1: Going to g3, your king moves away from the pawn and the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g3.2: The black king goes to d7 and then to c6, in front of the pawn: your king can no longer reach the key squares.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g2.1: Going to g2, your king retreats and moves away from the pawn and the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g2.2: The black king goes to d7 and then to c6, in front of the pawn: your king can no longer reach the key squares.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f2.1: Going to f2, your king retreats and wastes a move in the race to the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f2.2: The black king goes to d7 and then to c6, in front of the pawn: your king can no longer reach the key squares.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.b3b4.1: With the pawn on b4 before the king, the key squares move up to a6, b6 and c6: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.b3b4.2: The black king goes to d7, one step from c6; your king, on f3, is far from the new key squares.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v1.err.e4d4.1: Going to d4, your king goes to the black king's file, but leaves two squares between them: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v1.err.e4d4.2: An even number: the black king goes to d6, facing yours, and the direct opposition is his.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v2.err.d5c4.1: Going to c4, your king goes to the black king's file, but retreats and leaves two squares between them: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v2.err.d5c4.2: An even number: the black king goes to c6, facing yours, and shuts b5 and c5.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v3.err.b3b4.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: with it on b4, the key squares move up to a6, b6 and c6.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v3.err.b3b4.2: The black king goes to c7 and watches b6 and c6, the new key squares: it is a draw.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v4.err.b3b4.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: with it on b4, the key squares move up to a6, b6 and c6.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v4.err.b3b4.2: The black king goes to b7, in front of the pawn, and watches a6, b6 and c6: it is a draw.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v5.err.b5b6.1: Pushing the pawn now is too early: your king must get in front of it first.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.v5.err.b5b6.2: The black king goes to a8 and, when the pawn advances, steps back to b8, in front of it: it is a draw.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White and find the best move.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king went ahead with the distant opposition, and the pawn only advanced afterwards.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8d8.1: Going to d8, your king goes to the white king's file, but leaves six squares between them: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8d8.2: An even number: the opposition is White's. The white king goes to c2, toward the key squares a4, b4 and c4, ahead of yours.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8e7.1: Going to e7, your king advances off the white king's file and does not take the distant opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8e7.2: The white king goes to c2 and then to b3, next to the key squares a4, b4 and c4, before your king.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8f7.1: Going to f7, your king moves away from the pawn and does not take the distant opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8f7.2: The white king goes to c2 and then to b3, next to the key squares a4, b4 and c4, before your king.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8f8.1: Going to f8, your king retreats away from the pawn and does not take the distant opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.e8f8.2: The white king goes to c2 and then to b3, next to the key squares a4, b4 and c4, before your king.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d7c7.1: Going to c7, your king goes to the white king's file, but leaves four squares between them: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d7c7.2: An even number: the white king goes to b3, next to the key squares a4, b4 and c4, before your king.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d7d6.1: Going to d6, your king advances off the white king's file and does not take the distant opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v1.err.d7d6.2: The white king goes to b3, next to the key squares a4, b4 and c4, before your king.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v2.err.c6b6.1: Going to b6, your king goes to the white king's file, but leaves two squares between them: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v2.err.c6b6.2: An even number: the white king goes to b4, a key square, facing your king, and the direct opposition is his.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v2.err.c6c5.1: Going to c5, your king advances off the white king's file and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v2.err.c6c5.2: The white king goes to a4, a key square, before your king can watch it.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v2.err.c6b7.1: Going to b7, your king retreats and stays far from the key squares a4, b4 and c4: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v2.err.c6b7.2: The white king goes to b4, a key square, before your king.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v3.err.b5c4.1: Going to c4, your king leaves the white king's file and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.v3.err.b5c4.2: The white king goes to a4, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king took the distant opposition, five squares away: you had the tempo, and the white king did not get through.
